topic.source_contract: Brownfield register, previously developed land and permission-in-principle evidence

facts.register: LPAs prepare, maintain and publish registers of qualifying previously developed land
facts.parts: Part 1 records qualifying land; Part 2 can trigger permission in principle after statutory procedures
facts.guard: register inclusion alone is not a full planning permission or delivery record

facts.dataset: authoritative-source aggregation of brownfield register records
facts.fields: includes planning-permission status and site identifiers
facts.guard: national aggregation must be checked against the current local-authority record and exact geometry

facts.route: permission in principle may arise by application or Part 2 register entry
facts.scope: establishes core in-principle matters, with technical details handled separately
facts.guard: PiP is not technical-details consent, commencement approval or completed development

facts.standard: standardised publication fields for English brownfield registers
facts.guard: schema completeness does not prove current suitability, viability or implementation

facts.law: Town and Country Planning (Brownfield Land Register) Regulations 2017
facts.duty: requires registers of qualifying previously developed land
facts.guard: statutory criteria and local procedures must be applied to the exact current site record

scope_guards: Part 1 register entry is not treated as permission in principle.
Part 2 permission in principle is not treated as technical-details consent or full permission.
Previously developed land status is not treated as proof that every part of the red-line site is brownfield.
Register inclusion is not treated as proof of ownership, availability, viability or delivery.
An extant permission status is kept separate from implementation and completion.
National aggregated data is not substituted for the current local-authority record and exact boundary.
Brownfield classification is not treated as proof that land is contaminated or remediated.
No score or promotion is written without exact current register entry, geometry, planning status and decision evidence.
